ODU_083_Ìrosùn_Ọ̀kànràn.historical_timeline: Classical Ilé-Ifẹ̀ Antiquity (c. 9th–12th Century CE): Codified as Ìrosùn-Kànràn, teaching judicial truthfulness, courageous speech, and ancestral boundary defense. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́ Period (14th–18th Century CE): Consulted during high court trials by ordeal under Ṣàngó's priesthood. Transatlantic Survival: Preserved in Cuban and Brazilian Ifá archives as Iroso Kana, delivering initiates from false imprisonment and malicious slander.
ODU_083_Ìrosùn_Ọ̀kànràn.etymology_and_philosophy: Formed by pairing Ìrosùn (scarlet camwood, circulatory vitality, bloodline) on the right and Ọ̀kànràn (thunder, moral conviction, lightning speech) on the left of Ọpọ́n Ifá. Dialectically balances lineage memory with fearless judicial righteousness, demonstrating that ancestral honor must be defended through courageous moral speech.
ODU_083_Ìrosùn_Ọ̀kànràn.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed upon Ọpọ́n Ifá in two vertical columns: I/I/II/II on the right for Ìrosùn and II/II/II/I on the left for Ọ̀kànràn. Utilizes Osùn, Ẹdùn Àrá (thunderstone), Ewé Aragba, Ewé Ìná, and ram offerings to Ṣàngó.
ODU_083_Ìrosùn_Ọ̀kànràn.social_and_ritual_context: Divined during bitter court disputes, false criminal accusations, or ancestral boundary usurpations. Re-establishes justice and silences perjury.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìrosùn kànràn sọ òtítọ́ láì bẹ̀rù; àrá kì í pa ẹni tí kò hùwà ibi. (Ìrosùn Ọ̀kànràn proclaims the truth without fear; thunder never strikes down him who has committed no wickedness: Affirming absolute divine protection for the righteous.)

Bí a bá ń ja fún ẹ̀tọ́, a kì í fẹsẹ̀ fà sẹ́yìn; ọkàn líle la fi ń gbèjà ilé baba. (When fighting for justice, one does not retreat a step; stout-hearted courage is what defends the ancestral home: Inspiring steadfast defense of rights.)
A kì í fi irọ́ bo ojú ọ̀rọ̀; òtítọ́ inú ni Ọlọ́run ń gbé ga. (One does not conceal the truth beneath falsehood; it is inner integrity that the Almighty elevates: Condemning perjury in leadership.)
ODU_083_Ìrosùn_Ọ̀kànràn.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Barnes, Sandra T. (1997). Africa's Ogun: Old World and New.

ODU_084_Ìrosùn_Ògúndá.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ìrosùn-Gúndá or Ìrosùn-Dágò, governing metallurgy, surgical operations, and clearing obstacles from royal bloodlines. Imperial Era: Consulted by warrior chiefs before military expeditions. Diaspora Lineage: Retained in Lucumí patakís as Iroso Tolda under Ògún.
ODU_084_Ìrosùn_Ògúndá.etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ìrosùn (bloodline, life-force) and Ògúndá (Ògún's iron blade, cutting path). Teaches that historical and ancestral hindrances are decisively removed through technological labor, sacrifice, and iron resolve.
ODU_084_Ìrosùn_Ògúndá.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as I/I/II/II on the right and I/I/I/II on the left. Involves forged iron implements, Ewé Pèrègún, Ewé Ọ́kìkà, palm oil, and roasted yam offerings to Ògún.
ODU_084_Ìrosùn_Ògúndá.social_and_ritual_context: Employed before surgical procedures, hazardous travel, and large metallurgical undertakings. Safeguards workers from industrial accidents.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ògún la ọ̀nà fún Ìrosùn; irin kì í bẹ̀rù igbó tó kún fún ẹ̀gún. (Ògún cleared the path for Ìrosùn; forged iron harbors no fear of the briar-choked jungle: Celebrating technological and spiritual triumph.)

Ẹni tí ó mú ọ̀bẹ Ògún kì í fi bẹ́ orí ara rẹ̀; ọgbọ́n la fi ń lo agbára. (He who holds Ògún's sacred blade does not decapitate himself; wisdom must direct the application of force: Warning against reckless power.)

Bí a bá fẹ́ là ọ̀nà ọlá, iṣẹ́ ọwọ́ la fi ń bẹ̀rẹ̀; kò sí àṣeyọrí fún ọ̀lẹ. (If we seek to open the highway of majesty, skilled handiwork is the starting point; there is no victory for the slothful: Exhorting industrious labor.)
ODU_084_Ìrosùn_Ògúndá.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.

ODU_085_Ìrosùn_Ọ̀sá.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ìrosùn-Sá, governing protection against nocturnal astral predation, oneiromancy, and pacifying the spiritual Mothers. Imperial Era: Consulted by royal nurses to protect infant princes from astral hexes. Transatlantic Preservation: Documented in Cuban Ifá as Iroso Sa.
ODU_085_Ìrosùn_Ọ̀sá.etymology_and_philosophy: Synthesis of Ìrosùn (ancestral bloodline vitality) and Ọ̀sá (flight, nocturnal spirits, Ìyàmi). Teaches that the bloodline is shielded against nocturnal spiritual harm through respectful reconciliation with feminine cosmic forces.
ODU_085_Ìrosùn_Ọ̀sá.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/I/II/II on the right and II/I/I/I on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Ọ̀jìjí, Ewé Òdúndún, eggs, honey, and white hen offerings to the Mothers.
ODU_085_Ìrosùn_Ọ̀sá.social_and_ritual_context: Cast when a seeker is plagued by recurring nightmares, sleep paralysis, or unexplained blood ailments. Restores tranquil spiritual sleep.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìrosùn sá wọ àbò àwọn Ìyá, ó rí ìfọ̀kànbalẹ̀; ẹni tí àwọn àgbàlagbà bá gbè kì í sọnù. (Ìrosùn fled into the sanctuary of the Mothers and attained deep tranquility; he whom the elder matriarchs endorse never perishes: Commending maternal spiritual peace.)

Ẹyẹ kì í fò kí ó gbàgbé orí igi; bí a bá rìn jìnnà tó, orísun la ó padà sí. (The bird never flies so far as to forget the tree canopy; however far we journey, to our ancestral origin we must return: Teaching loyalty to roots.)

Bí afẹ́fẹ́ bá ń jà, a kì í fi ilé sílẹ̀ láì ti ilẹ̀kùn; ìṣọ́ra ni odi awo. (When astral winds blow, one does not leave the home unbarred; spiritual vigilance is the fortress of the initiate: Preaching preventive protection.)
ODU_085_Ìrosùn_Ọ̀sá.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Lawal, Babatunde (1996). The Gelede Spectacle; Washington, Teresa N. (2005). Our Mothers, Our Powers, Our Texts.

ODU_086_Ìrosùn_Ìká.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ìrosùn-Ká, governing the neutralizing of domestic poisons, coiling malicious gossip, and curing venomous inflammation. Imperial Era: Consulted in court when food poisoning of royalty was suspected. Diaspora Survival: Preserved in Lucumí Ifá as Iroso Ka.
ODU_086_Ìrosùn_Ìká.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìrosùn (lineage life-force) with Ìká (restraint, coiling venom). Teaches that envious malice aimed at the bloodline is disarmed through composed moral restraint and physical detoxifying hygiene.
ODU_086_Ìrosùn_Ìká.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked as I/I/II/II on the right and II/I/II/II on the left on Ìyẹ̀rosùn. Involves cooling shea butter (Òrí), Ewé Ègé, Ewé Arújẹ, and white pigeon sacrifice.
ODU_086_Ìrosùn_Ìká.social_and_ritual_context: Divined when someone is surrounded by jealous peers or insidious slander. Commands calmness, discretion, and clean hands.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìrosùn ká ọwọ́ ìkà kúrò lórí awo; ẹni tó gbẹ́ kòtò kì í rí awo gbé ṣe. (Ìrosùn bound the hands of malice from the initiate; he who digs a pit finds no power to snare the righteous: Proclaiming victory over covert traps.)

Ìkà kò mọ̀ pé Ọlọ́run ń wo ilẹ̀; ìwà rere ni àbò tí kò lè wó. (The wicked plotter forgets that the Creator surveys the earth; righteous character is an indestructible fortress: Warning against deceit.)
A kì í fi ọwọ́ méjì gba ejò sí abíyá; awo tó fojú fò kì í jẹ oró. (One does not embrace a viper into one's bosom; an alert initiate never tastes bitter venom: Demanding strict boundary-setting.)
ODU_086_Ìrosùn_Ìká.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.

ODU_087_Ìrosùn_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ìrosùn-Túúrúpọ̀n or Ìrosùn-Tọmọpọ̀n, celebrating infant pediatrics, safe deliveries, and maternal blood protection. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́: Favored by palace matrons supervising royal nurseries. Transatlantic Resilience: Maintained in Cuban Ifá as Iroso Batrupon.
ODU_087_Ìrosùn_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìrosùn (lifeblood, lineage memory) with Òtúúrúpọ̀n (carrying children upon the back, maternal care). Teaches that the continuity of human civilization rests upon nurturing vulnerable youth and honoring the labor of mothers.
ODU_087_Ìrosùn_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/I/II/II on the right and II/II/I/II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Àbáwẹ̀, Ewé Ọ̀já-Ọmọ, cold maize gruel (Ẹ̀kọ), and snail broth.
ODU_087_Ìrosùn_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.social_and_ritual_context: Cast for pediatric care, midwives, pregnant women, and civic leaders bearing collective community burdens. Protects young children.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìrosùn pọ̀n ọmọ mọ́ra, ó ti ẹnu-ọ̀nà àrùn; ọmọ lúwàbí kì í kú ní kékeré. (Ìrosùn strapped the infant to its back and locked the gate against illness; a child of destiny shall not perish in youth: Celebrating pediatric preservation.)

Ẹrù ọmọ kì í pa ìyá rẹ̀; ìfẹ́ inú la fi ń gbé iran tó ń bọ̀ ga. (The burden of an infant never breaks the mother's back; it is with devoted love that we elevate the generation to come: Praising maternal fortitude.)

A kì í fi ọmọdé dá ogun sílẹ̀; àwọn ọmọ wẹẹrẹ ni adé àlàáfíà ilé. (One does not endanger little children in community strife; young children are the crown of domestic peace: Mandating child protection.)
ODU_087_Ìrosùn_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Fadipe, N.A. (1970). The Sociology of the Yoruba.

ODU_088_Ìrosùn_Òtúá.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ìrosùn-Túá, governing the release of ancestral captives, spiritual covenant, and inter-religious tolerance. Imperial Era: Consulted when ratifying non-aggression treaties. Transatlantic Retention: Documented in Lucumí Ifá as Iroso Tura.
ODU_088_Ìrosùn_Òtúá.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìrosùn (bloodline honor) with Òtúá (prayer, release, covenant). Teaches that freedom and peace arrive when ancestral grievances are released through sincere prayer and covenantal reconciliation.
ODU_088_Ìrosùn_Òtúá.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as I/I/II/II on the right and I/II/I/I on the left. Involves Ewé Ẹfun, Ewé Tètè, white dove, honey, and white chalk (Ẹfun).
ODU_088_Ìrosùn_Òtúá.social_and_ritual_context: Cast during treaty ratifications, prisoner releases, and personal prayers for emancipation from spiritual bondage.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìrosùn tú àwọ̀n sílẹ̀, ó fi òmìnira wọ ìlú; ẹni tí ó ba gbé àlàáfíà ga kì í rí ogun. (Ìrosùn dismantled the snare and entered the city with freedom; he who exalts peace never faces warfare: Celebrating liberty and peace.)

Àdúrà tí a fi ọkàn mímọ́ gbà kì í ṣubú sílẹ̀; Ọlọ́run ń gbèjà olódodo. (The prayer offered with a pure conscience never falls flat; the Supreme Being defends the upright: Affirming divine deliverance.)

A kì í fi odi dí ọ̀nà àtiwọ ìmọ́lẹ̀; sùúrù la fi ń gbádùn àṣẹ àwọn àgbà. (One does not erect a wall to shut out the incoming light; it is with patience that one receives the blessings of the elders: Encouraging openness to truth.)
ODU_088_Ìrosùn_Òtúá.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.

ODU_089_Ìrosùn_Ìrẹtẹ̀.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ìrosùn-Rẹtẹ̀ or Ìrosùn-Ate, governing the conquest of bone maladies, chronic infirmities, and humiliating skin conditions. Imperial Era: Consulted by priest-physicians during smallpox epidemics. Diaspora Lineage: Retained in Cuban Ifá as Iroso Ate under Ọbalúayé.
ODU_089_Ìrosùn_Ìrẹtẹ̀.etymology_and_philosophy: Synthesis of Ìrosùn (lifeblood) and Ìrẹtẹ̀ (humility, earth, physical healing). Teaches that physical healing is achieved when human arrogance yields to therapeutic natural medicine and ecological balance.
ODU_089_Ìrosùn_Ìrẹtẹ̀.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/I/II/II on the right and I/I/II/I on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Ìrẹtẹ̀, Ewé Gbégbé, roasted cornmeal, and palm wine for Ọbalúayé.
ODU_089_Ìrosùn_Ìrẹtẹ̀.social_and_ritual_context: Cast for patients suffering from dermatological ulcers, joint stiffness, or societal rejection. Demands strict hygiene and humility.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìrosùn rẹtẹ̀ mọ́lẹ̀, ó wo gbogbo àrùn sàn; àṣẹ Ọbalúayé kì í ṣe ohun àbùkù. (Ìrosùn bowed low to the earth and healed all diseases; the authority of Ọbalúayé is never an object of shame: Praising divine healing through humility.)

Ẹni tí ó tẹríba kì í tẹ́ nígbà ìpọ́njú; ìlera ni baba ọrọ̀. (He who bows his head never suffers humiliation during tribulation; vibrant health is the father of all wealth: Prioritizing health over vanity.)

A kì í fi ìgbéraga kọ ẹbọ ìwòsàn; ẹni tó fẹ́ gbádùn gbọ́dọ̀ gba ìmọ̀ràn àgbà. (One does not reject therapeutic sacrifice through arrogance; he who desires long life must heed elder counsel: Urging medical compliance.)
ODU_089_Ìrosùn_Ìrẹtẹ̀.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.

ODU_090_Ìrosùn_Ọ̀ṣẹ́.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ìrosùn-Ṣẹ́, celebrating feminine grace, riverine wealth, and triumphant breakthrough from grief. Imperial Era: Consulted before royal festive banquets. Diaspora Survival: Maintained in Lucumí Ifá as Iroso She under Ọ̀ṣun.
ODU_090_Ìrosùn_Ọ̀ṣẹ́.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìrosùn (bloodline honor, camwood) with Ọ̀ṣẹ́ (victory, sweetness, riverine joy). Demonstrates that lineage sorrows are sweetened and elevated when touched by Ọ̀ṣun's fertile blessing.
ODU_090_Ìrosùn_Ọ̀ṣẹ́.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as I/I/II/II on the right and I/II/I/II on the left. Involves Ewé Rinrin, Ewé Àjẹ́obàlé, river stones, brass bangles, and honey for Ọ̀ṣun.
ODU_090_Ìrosùn_Ọ̀ṣẹ́.social_and_ritual_context: Divined for seekers suffering long periods of sorrow, depression, or commercial failure. Restores marital and financial vitality.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìrosùn ṣẹ́gun ọ̀tá, ó fi oyin kún inú ilé; ayọ̀ ń bẹ fún ẹni tí ó ba nífẹ̀ẹ́ sí Ọ̀ṣun. (Ìrosùn vanquished the adversary and filled the house with honey; boundless joy awaits him who walks in covenant with Ọ̀ṣun: Celebrating fertile victory.)

Omi tútù kì í pọ́n lójú àgbàrá; ẹni tí ó ní sùúrù yóò jẹ adùn ayé. (Clear river water never turns muddy in the presence of seasonal flooding; he who possesses patience shall taste the sweetness of life: Preaching perseverance.)

Bí a bá ń wá ọlá, a gbọ́dọ̀ wẹ ọwọ́ mọ́; ìmọ́tótó ni baba àṣeyọrí. (If we seek majesty, we must wash our hands clean; immaculate purity is the foundation of triumph: Emphasizing clean ethics in wealth creation.)
ODU_090_Ìrosùn_Ọ̀ṣẹ́.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Abiodun, Rowland (2014). Yoruba Art and Language.

ODU_091_Ìrosùn_Òfún.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ìrosùn-Fún, the sacred chapter where ancestral camwood bloodlines are crowned in Ọbàtálá's pure white light. Imperial Era: Consulted during royal coronations. Diaspora Lineage: Preserved in Cuban Ifá as Iroso Fumbo.
ODU_091_Ìrosùn_Òfún.etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ìrosùn (bloodline memory) and Òfún (divine white creation, Ọbàtálá). Encapsulates the complete transfiguration of generational curses into immaculate spiritual authority and peaceful longevity.
ODU_091_Ìrosùn_Òfún.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/I/II/II on the right and II/I/II/I on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with pristine white pigeons, Ẹfun (chalk), Ewé Ọ̀bàtálá, and shea butter.
ODU_091_Ìrosùn_Òfún.social_and_ritual_context: Cast during deep identity crises, severe disputes, or ancestral crossroad determinations. Cleanses spiritual pollution and grants tranquil authority.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìrosùn fún funfun gba adé Ọbàtálá, gbogbo ibi di ìmọ́lẹ̀; ikú kì í pa awo funfun. (Ìrosùn shone in immaculate white and received the crown of Ọbàtálá, transforming all darkness into radiance; death never claims the pristine initiate: Announcing spiritual transfiguration.)

Àlà funfun kì í dọ̀tí lójú Ọlọ́run; ẹni tí ó mọ́ ọkàn ni àpótí ọlá. (White linen never soils before the Creator; he who maintains a clean conscience is the treasury of majesty: Praising moral purity.)

Ẹni tí ó ru ẹbọ Òfún ti di odi mọ́ gbogbo ibi; a kì í fi ìméjì bọ Òrìṣà. (He who makes the sacrifice of Òfún has walled off all wickedness; one must not serve the divinities with double-mindedness: Demanding sincere devotion.)
ODU_091_Ìrosùn_Òfún.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Idowu, E. Bolaji (1962). Olodumare: God in Yoruba Belief.

ODU_092_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ogbè.historical_timeline: Classical Ilé-Ifẹ̀ Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Sogbè or Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Ogbè, celebrated for transforming trade whirlwinds into boundless expansion and wealth. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́: Favored by caravans crossing imperial frontiers. Transatlantic Resilience: Documented in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Shobe.
ODU_092_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ogbè.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀wọ́nrín (whirlwind, sudden commerce, scarcity) on the right with Ogbè (cosmic radiance, expansion) on the left. Demonstrates that economic volatility and market fluctuations turn into monumental prosperity when guided by the radiant light of truth.
ODU_092_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ogbè.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and I on the left. Involves Ewé Ajé, Ewé Ṣaworo-pẹ́pẹ́, cowries, bananas, honey, and white rooster offerings.
ODU_092_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ogbè.social_and_ritual_context: Cast during unpredictable commercial shifts or when launching major entrepreneurial ventures. Bestows commercial breakthrough.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín sogbè sọ owó di púpọ̀; oòrùn owúrọ̀ kì í pa olówó tì. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín Sogbè multiplied wealth into abundance; the morning sun never fails the industrious laborer: Celebrating commercial triumph through diligence.)

Afẹ́fẹ́ kì í gbé ilé tí a fi òtítọ́ kọ́ lọ; awo tó mọ ìwà rẹ̀ kì í ṣubú. (The tempest never blows away a home founded upon truth; an initiate conscious of his character never falls: Affirming foundational stability.)

Bí a bá ń wá ajé, a kì í fi ẹ̀tàn gba owó lọ́wọ́ ará; ìwà rere ni baba ọrọ̀. (When seeking wealth, one does not swindle one's neighbor; righteous conduct is the true father of riches: Preaching commercial honesty.)
ODU_092_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ogbè.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.

ODU_093_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Yẹ̀kú, governing the pacification of destructive tempests, averting sudden mortality, and clearing ancestral debts. Imperial Era: Consulted during outbreaks of drought or famine. Diaspora Lineage: Retained in Cuban Ifá as Ojuani Yekun.
ODU_093_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú.etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (whirlwind, instability) and Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (darkness, mortal transition). Teaches that the turbulent storms of physical existence are quelled through quiet ancestral contemplation and sacrificial propitiation.
ODU_093_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/I/I on the right and II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Ọ̀dúndún, Ewé Tètè, black ram offering, and cool well water.
ODU_093_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú.social_and_ritual_context: Divined during sudden community epidemics, family bereavement, or natural catastrophes. Quells panic and anchors communal peace.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín yẹ̀kú ti ẹnu-ọ̀nà ikú; afẹ́fẹ́ burúkú kì í fẹ́ wọ ilé awo. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀yẹ̀kú shut the portal of death; the malevolent gale never penetrates the home of the initiate: Proclaiming immunity from catastrophe.)

Ẹni tó bọ orí rẹ̀ ti la ewu kọjá; a kì í fi ẹ̀mí ṣeré nínú ìjì. (He who propitiates his own inner head has survived peril; one must never gamble with sacred life amidst the tempest: Prioritizing spiritual self-care.)

Bí òkùnkùn bá kù sẹ́yìn, ìmọ́lẹ̀ Ifá a yọ; sùúrù la fi ń rí àlàáfíà. (Though darkness lingers, the radiant light of Ifá shall appear; it is with patience that one receives enduring peace: Giving hope during grief.)
ODU_093_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀yẹ̀kú.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.

ODU_094_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìwòrì.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Wòrì, governing financial foresight, navigating fluctuating commodity markets, and avoiding contractual traps. Imperial Era: Consulted by merchants before entering interstate treaties. Diaspora Preservation: Documented in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Tanshela.
ODU_094_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìwòrì.etymology_and_philosophy: Synthesis of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (market vortex, trade) and Ìwòrì (spiritual sight, retrospection). Teaches that business volatility is mastered when foresight, historical analysis, and sharp vision guide economic choices.
ODU_094_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìwòrì.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and II/I/I/II on the left. Involves Ewé Ajé, Ewé Pèrègún, cowries, and honey offerings.
ODU_094_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìwòrì.social_and_ritual_context: Cast when entering significant financial partnerships or recovering from market panics. Demands sharp analytical auditing.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín wòrì wo iwájú ọjà, ó rí ajé; ojú tó ṣí sílẹ̀ kì í kùnà. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ìwòrì surveyed the marketplace and seized prosperity; the open, vigilant eye never misses auspicious opportunities: Praising commercial foresight.)

A kì í fi owó ọjà bọ Òrìṣà láìní ìròyìn; ìṣirò pípé ni baba ọrọ̀. (One does not expend commercial capital upon ritual without accounting; rigorous bookkeeping is the father of wealth: Teaching fiscal discipline.)
Bí afẹ́fẹ́ bá ń fẹ́, awo gbọ́dọ̀ wo ibi tí eruku ń lọ; ìwòrì kì í kọsẹ̀. (When the wind blows, the initiate observes where the dust settles; true foresight never stumbles: Warning against blindness.)
ODU_094_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìwòrì.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Fatunmbi, Awo Fa'lokun (1992). Iwa-Pele: Ifa Quest.

ODU_095_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òdí.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Dí, governing the defensive containment of market earnings, boundary protection, and stopping leakages. Imperial Era: Consulted by royal treasurers to prevent embezzlement. Diaspora Lineage: Maintained in Cuban Ifá as Ojuani Bodi.
ODU_095_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òdí.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade windfall, whirlwind) with Òdí (rampart, container, seal). Teaches that rapid financial gains are useless unless contained within disciplined reserve systems and protected against waste.
ODU_095_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òdí.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/I/I on the right and I/II/II/I on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Ètìpọ́nlà, Ewé Gbégbé, black soap, and sealed earthen vessels.
ODU_095_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òdí.social_and_ritual_context: Divined when money disappears mysteriously, or when a business suffers from unexplained financial drain. Fortifies savings.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín dí àpò owó, ó ti ẹnu-ọ̀nà àbùkù; owó awo kì í sọnù sínú eruku. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín sealed the purse of wealth and shut the gate on shame; the initiate's earnings never vanish into dust: Celebrating financial containment.)

Odi tí a fi sùúrù mọ kì í jẹ́ kí ajé tú ká; awo tó mọ iṣẹ́ ṣe kì í ráhùn. (A wall constructed with patience never allows wealth to scatter; an industrious initiate never laments of poverty: Emphasizing disciplined savings.)

A kì í fi àpò tó ya kójọ owó; pẹ̀lẹ́pẹ̀lẹ́ la fi ń rán aṣọ ọlá. (One does not collect currency within a torn pouch; it is with gentle care that robes of majesty are stitched: Warning against careless waste.)
ODU_095_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òdí.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.

ODU_096_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìrosùn.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Rosùn, governing lineage commerce, preserving ancestral estates, and avoiding spendthrift ruin. Imperial Era: Consulted when settling estate inheritances. Diaspora Survival: Documented in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Hermoso.
ODU_096_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìrosùn.etymology_and_philosophy: Synthesis of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade winds, scarcity) and Ìrosùn (camwood, bloodline honor). Demonstrates that ancestral heritage is sustained when commercial earnings are reinvested to honor family bloodlines.
ODU_096_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìrosùn.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and I/I/II/II on the left. Involves Osùn, Ewé Ọ́kìkà, Ewé Ajé, honey, and guinea fowl sacrifice.
ODU_096_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìrosùn.social_and_ritual_context: Cast when family estates are squandered by reckless heirs. Prescribes family council mediation and ancestral rededication.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín rosùn sọ owó di púpọ̀, ó fi ọlá bo ilé; afẹ́fẹ́ kì í gbé olóye lọ. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ìrosùn multiplied wealth into abundance and clothed the home in majesty; the gale never carries away the wise thinker: Celebrating fiscal resilience.)

Owó kì í wọ ilé láì ní làálàá; awo tó gbọ́n kì í fi ọjọ́ ọrọ̀ gbàgbé ọjọ́ ebi. (Wealth never enters the home without honest labor; a wise initiate never forgets the days of famine during times of abundance: Preaching economic foresight.)

Bí ìjì bá ń jà, a kì í bọ́ sínú ọjà láìní ẹ̀ṣọ́; ìṣirò rere ni baba ajé. (When the storm rages, one does not venture to the market without protection; careful accounting is the father of wealth: Demanding fiscal discipline.)
ODU_096_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìrosùn.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.

ODU_097_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀bàrà.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Bàrà, celebrated for eloquence in trade diplomacy, settling market strikes, and royal mercantile wealth. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́: Favored by the Ìyál'óde in trade negotiations. Diaspora Retention: Maintained in Cuban Ifá as Ojuani Bara.
ODU_097_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀bàrà.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade vortex, wealth) with Ọ̀bàrà (manifestation, royal speech, kingship). Teaches that fair business diplomacy and honest speech convert mercantile profits into lasting royal prestige.
ODU_097_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀bàrà.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/I/I on the right and I/II/II/II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Àkòko, Ewé Ẹ̀lẹ́gẹdẹ, rooster, and white cowries.
ODU_097_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀bàrà.social_and_ritual_context: Cast for traders, guild leaders, and statesmen negotiating complex financial contracts. Inculcates fair dealing and eloquence.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín bàrà sọ ọ̀rọ̀ ọjà di oyin; ahọ́n rere ní ń fa ọlá mọ́ra. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀bàrà turned market speech into sweet honey; an eloquent, honest tongue is that which attracts majesty: Exalting diplomatic rhetoric.)
Ẹni tí ayé kẹ́gàn ní àná ló ń jẹ ọba lónìí; Ifá kì í fi olódodo sílẹ̀. (He whom the world mocked yesterday is crowned king today; Ifá never abandons the upright: Encouraging perseverance.)

A kì í fi irọ́ kọ́ ààfin ọlá; òtítọ́ inú nìkan ló lè gbé adé dúró lórí. (One does not erect the palace of majesty upon lies; only inner truthfulness can sustain the crown upon the head: Demanding ethical leadership.)
ODU_097_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀bàrà.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.

ODU_098_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀kànràn.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Kànràn, embodying lightning courage in commercial disputes, defending market rights, and repelling extortion. Imperial Era: Consulted during market guild revolts. Diaspora Lineage: Documented in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Pokon.
ODU_098_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀kànràn.etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade turbulence) and Ọ̀kànràn (thunder, moral conviction). Teaches that economic extortion must be courageously resisted; compromise with thieves destroys civic commerce.
ODU_098_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀kànràn.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and II/II/II/I on the left. Involves Ẹdùn Àrá, Ewé Aragba, Ewé Ìná, and ram offerings for Ṣàngó.
ODU_098_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀kànràn.social_and_ritual_context: Divined when merchants face extortion, racketeering, or violent seizure of property. Invokes Ṣàngó's protective justice.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín kànràn sọ òtítọ́ láì bẹ̀rù; àrá kì í pa ẹni tí kò hùwà ibi. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀kànràn proclaims the truth without fear; thunder never strikes down him who has committed no wickedness: Affirming divine defense.)

Bí a bá ń ja fún ẹ̀tọ́, a kì í fẹsẹ̀ fà sẹ́yìn; ọkàn líle la fi ń gbèjà ọjà. (When fighting for our rights, one does not retreat a step; stout-hearted courage is what defends the marketplace: Inspiring commercial justice.)

A kì í fi ìbínú gbin ẹ̀wọ̀n sí ilẹ̀; ìwà pẹ̀lẹ́ ni olórí gbogbo ogun. (One does not plant thorns of wrath in the soil; gentle self-control is the master of all conflict: Warning against hot-headedness.)
ODU_098_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀kànràn.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Barnes, Sandra T. (1997). Africa's Ogun: Old World and New.

ODU_099_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ògúndá.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Gúndá or Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Dágò, governing transport technology, blacksmithing commerce, and clearing road blockades. Imperial Era: Consulted by caravan toll collectors and blacksmith guilds. Diaspora Preservation: Retained in Cuban Ifá as Ojuani Dawan.
ODU_099_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ògúndá.etymology_and_philosophy: Synthesis of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (commerce, trade movement) and Ògúndá (iron, path-clearing). Demonstrates that trade routes flourish and commerce expands when backed by robust iron technology and secure roadways.
ODU_099_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ògúndá.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/I/I on the right and I/I/I/II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Pèrègún, Ewé Ọ́kìkà, forged iron nails, and roasted yam offerings.
ODU_099_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ògúndá.social_and_ritual_context: Cast for merchants embarking upon perilous long-distance trade or builders constructing commercial infrastructure.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ògún ti ọ̀nà ọjà pẹ̀lú irin, kò sí olè tó lè wọlé; àdá kì í wọ igbó lásán. (Ògún secured the trade route with forged iron, no thief can enter; the cutlass never enters the forest in vain: Celebrating trade security.)

Ẹni tí ó ń lu irin nínú àrọ kì í bẹ̀rù iná; iṣẹ́ ọwọ́ la fi ń di akọni. (He who hammers iron in the forge harbors no fear of sparks; it is through technical craft that heroes are made: Elevating metallurgical craftsmanship.)

A kì í fi irin dá ogun sí ara wa; àṣẹ Ògún wà fún àbò kì í ṣe fún ìparun. (One does not turn iron weapons upon one's own kin; Ògún's authority is given for protection, not senseless destruction: Demanding ethical tool usage.)
ODU_099_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ògúndá.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.

ODU_100_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀sá.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Sá, governing protection against sudden financial collapse, market fires, and placating nocturnal astral societies. Imperial Era: Consulted when fires broke out in large urban markets. Diaspora Survival: Preserved in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Boshe.
ODU_100_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀sá.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade vortex) with Ọ̀sá (flight, sudden wind, astral spirits). Teaches that commercial wealth is vulnerable to sudden disasters; peace and fortune are safeguarded through respectful appeasement of the cosmic Mothers.
ODU_100_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀sá.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and II/I/I/I on the left. Involves Ewé Ọ̀jìjí, Ewé Òdúndún, eggs, honey, and white hen offerings to Ìyàmi.
ODU_100_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀sá.social_and_ritual_context: Divined after commercial fires, sudden financial ruin, or severe nocturnal anxiety. Restores financial and emotional equilibrium.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín sá wọ àbò àwọn Ìyá, ó rí ìfọ̀kànbalẹ̀; ẹni tí àwọn àgbàlagbà bá gbè kì í sọnù. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín fled into the sanctuary of the Mothers and attained deep tranquility; he whom the elder matriarchs endorse never perishes: Commending spiritual sanctuary.)

Ẹyẹ kì í kọ odi tí a fi oyin kọ́; àlàáfíà ń bẹ fún ẹni tó bọ̀wọ̀ fún àwọn Ìyá. (The bird of the night never attacks a rampart consecrated with honey; peace reigns for him who honors the Mothers: Emphasizing gentle diplomacy with spiritual powers.)

Bí afẹ́fẹ́ bá ń jà, a kì í fi ilé sílẹ̀ láì ti ilẹ̀kùn; ìṣọ́ra ni odi awo. (When astral gales blow, one does not leave the dwelling unbarred; spiritual vigilance is the fortress of the initiate: Preaching preventive protection.)
ODU_100_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀sá.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Lawal, Babatunde (1996). The Gelede Spectacle; Washington, Teresa N. (2005). Our Mothers, Our Powers, Our Texts.

ODU_101_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìká.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Ká, governing the neutralizing of commercial fraud, contractual perjury, and stopping envious backbiters. Imperial Era: Consulted during market price-fixing disputes. Diaspora Lineage: Documented in Cuban Ifá as Ojuani Bika.
ODU_101_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìká.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade, movement) with Ìká (restraint, coiling venom). Teaches that the poison of commercial fraud is disarmed through rigorous contractual transparency and refusal to participate in corrupt schemes.
ODU_101_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìká.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/I/I on the right and II/I/II/II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Ègé, Ewé Arújẹ, cooling shea butter, and white pigeon offerings.
ODU_101_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìká.social_and_ritual_context: Cast when a business person is targeted by envious competitors or malicious audits. Commands absolute transparency and serene restraint.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín ká ọwọ́ ìkà kúrò lórí awo; ẹni tó gbẹ́ kòtò kì í rí awo gbé ṣe. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín bound the hands of malice from the initiate; he who digs a pit finds no power to snare the righteous: Proclaiming victory over covert traps.)

Ìkà kò mọ̀ pé Ọlọ́run ń wo ilẹ̀; ìwà rere ni àbò tí kò lè wó. (The wicked plotter forgets that the Creator surveys the earth; righteous character is an indestructible fortress: Warning against deceit.)

A kì í fi ọwọ́ méjì gbá odi ẹjọ́ mú; sùúrù la fi ń tu àwọ̀n tí ó kọ́. (One does not dismantle an entangled dispute with violent fury; it is with patience that one untangles the knotted net: Recommending patient conflict resolution.)
ODU_101_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìká.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.

ODU_102_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Túúrúpọ̀n, governing family welfare, supporting expectant mothers, and managing domestic provisions during scarcity. Imperial Era: Consulted during food rationing in sieges. Diaspora Retention: Maintained in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Batrupon.
ODU_102_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade provisions) and Òtúúrúpọ̀n (maternal care, carrying on the back). Teaches that during times of economic scarcity, communal solidarity and priority care for children guarantee civilizational survival.
ODU_102_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and II/II/I/II on the left. Involves Ewé Àbáwẹ̀, Ewé Ọ̀já-Ọmọ, cold maize gruel (Ẹ̀kọ), and snail broth.
ODU_102_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.social_and_ritual_context: Cast for families managing scarce food supplies, pediatric clinics, and maternity wards. Strengthens domestic resilience.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín pọ̀n ọmọ mọ́ra, ó ti ẹnu-ọ̀nà àrùn; ọmọ lúwàbí kì í kú ní kékeré. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín strapped the infant to its back and locked the gate against illness; a child of destiny shall not perish in youth: Celebrating pediatric preservation.)

Ẹrù ọmọ kì í pa ìyá rẹ̀; ìfẹ́ inú la fi ń gbé iran tó ń bọ̀ ga. (The burden of an infant never breaks the mother's back; it is with devoted love that we elevate the generation to come: Praising maternal fortitude.)

A kì í fi ọmọdé dá ogun sílẹ̀; àwọn ọmọ wẹẹrẹ ni adé àlàáfíà ilé. (One does not endanger little children in community strife; young children are the crown of domestic peace: Mandating child protection.)
ODU_102_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òtúúrúpọ̀n.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Fadipe, N.A. (1970). The Sociology of the Yoruba.

ODU_103_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òtúá.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Túá, governing commercial treaties, release of bonded debtors, and peaceful trade pacts. Imperial Era: Consulted when lifting interstate trade embargoes. Transatlantic Survival: Preserved in Cuban Ifá as Ojuani Alakentu.
ODU_103_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òtúá.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade movement, whirlwind) with Òtúá (prayer, release, covenant). Teaches that prosperous commerce thrives only where peace covenants are upheld and bonded debts are mercifully restructured.
ODU_103_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òtúá.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/I/I on the right and I/II/I/I on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Ẹfun, Ewé Tètè, white dove, honey, and white chalk (Ẹfun).
ODU_103_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òtúá.social_and_ritual_context: Cast during treaty ratifications, debt forgiveness arbitrations, and prayers for freedom from financial bondage.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín tú àwọ̀n sílẹ̀, ó fi òmìnira wọ ìlú; ẹni tí ó ba gbé àlàáfíà ga kì í rí ogun. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín dismantled the snare and entered the city with freedom; he who exalts peace never faces warfare: Celebrating liberty and peace.)

Àdúrà tí a fi ọkàn mímọ́ gbà kì í ṣubú sílẹ̀; Ọlọ́run ń gbèjà olódodo. (The prayer offered with a pure conscience never falls flat; the Supreme Being defends the upright: Affirming divine deliverance.)

A kì í fi odi dí ọ̀nà àtiwọ ìmọ́lẹ̀; sùúrù la fi ń gbádùn àṣẹ àwọn àgbà. (One does not erect a wall to shut out the incoming light; it is with patience that one receives the blessings of the elders: Encouraging openness to truth.)
ODU_103_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òtúá.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.

ODU_104_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìrẹtẹ̀.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Rẹtẹ̀, governing the conquest of economic contagions, bone maladies, and curing commercial disgrace. Imperial Era: Consulted during agrarian plagues. Diaspora Lineage: Retained in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Birete under Ọbalúayé.
ODU_104_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìrẹtẹ̀.etymology_and_philosophy: Synthesis of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade instability) and Ìrẹtẹ̀ (humility, earth, convalescence). Teaches that economic and physical plagues are healed when human society practices radical humility, ecological stewardship, and sanitation.
ODU_104_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìrẹtẹ̀.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and I/I/II/I on the left. Involves Ewé Ìrẹtẹ̀, Ewé Gbégbé, roasted cornmeal, and palm wine for Ọbalúayé.
ODU_104_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìrẹtẹ̀.social_and_ritual_context: Cast for people suffering from sudden poverty, dermatological infections, or social ruin. Commands humility and strict environmental hygiene.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín rẹtẹ̀ mọ́lẹ̀, ó wo gbogbo àrùn sàn; àṣẹ Ọbalúayé kì í ṣe ohun àbùkù. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín bowed low to the earth and healed all diseases; the authority of Ọbalúayé is never an object of shame: Praising divine healing through humility.)

Ẹni tí ó tẹríba kì í tẹ́ nígbà ìpọ́njú; ìlera ni baba ọrọ̀. (He who bows his head never suffers humiliation during tribulation; vibrant health is the father of all wealth: Prioritizing health over vanity.)

A kì í fi ìgbéraga kọ ẹbọ ìwòsàn; ẹni tó fẹ́ gbádùn gbọ́dọ̀ gba ìmọ̀ràn àgbà. (One does not reject therapeutic sacrifice through arrogance; he who desires long life must heed elder counsel: Urging medical compliance.)
ODU_104_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ìrẹtẹ̀.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.

ODU_105_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀ṣẹ́.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Ṣẹ́, celebrating the sweet victory of trade, riverine wealth, and banishing financial anxiety. Imperial Era: Consulted before royal markets opened in the capital. Diaspora Preservation: Documented in Cuban Ifá as Ojuani Boshe under Ọ̀ṣun.
ODU_105_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀ṣẹ́.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade movement, whirlwind) with Ọ̀ṣẹ́ (victory, sweetness, riverine joy). Teaches that the turbulent labor of commerce blossoms into overflowing joy and wealth when crowned with maternal sweetness and ethical beauty.
ODU_105_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀ṣẹ́.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/I/I on the right and I/II/I/II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Rinrin, Ewé Àjẹ́obàlé, river stones, brass ornaments, and honey for Ọ̀ṣun.
ODU_105_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀ṣẹ́.social_and_ritual_context: Divined for merchants suffering from chronic trade depression or reproductive delay. Restores vibrant joy and commercial fertility.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín ṣẹ́gun ọ̀tá, ó fi oyin kún inú ilé; ayọ̀ ń bẹ fún ẹni tí ó ba nífẹ̀ẹ́ sí Ọ̀ṣun. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín vanquished the adversary and filled the house with honey; boundless joy awaits him who walks in covenant with Ọ̀ṣun: Celebrating fertile victory.)

Omi tútù kì í pọ́n lójú àgbàrá; ẹni tí ó ní sùúrù yóò jẹ adùn ayé. (Clear river water never turns muddy in the presence of seasonal flooding; he who possesses patience shall taste the sweetness of life: Preaching perseverance.)

Bí a bá ń wá ọlá, a gbọ́dọ̀ wẹ ọwọ́ mọ́; ìmọ́tótó ni baba àṣeyọrí. (If we seek majesty, we must wash our hands clean; immaculate purity is the foundation of triumph: Emphasizing clean ethics in wealth creation.)
ODU_105_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Ọ̀ṣẹ́.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Abiodun, Rowland (2014). Yoruba Art and Language.

ODU_106_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òfún.historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Fún, the sacred chapter where financial whirlwinds are sanctified in Ọbàtálá's pure white light. Imperial Era: Consulted during state coronations to secure agricultural abundance. Diaspora Survival: Preserved in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Bofun.
ODU_106_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òfún.etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (whirlwind, commerce) and Òfún (divine white creation, Ọbàtálá). Encapsulates the complete transfiguration of earthly commercial struggles into immaculate spiritual authority, clean riches, and eternal peace.
ODU_106_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òfún.material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and II/I/II/I on the left. Involves pristine white pigeons, Ẹfun (chalk), Ewé Ọ̀bàtálá, and shea butter.
ODU_106_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òfún.social_and_ritual_context: Cast during profound identity crossroads, deep financial crises, or spiritual disorientation. Cleanses corrupt stains and grants serene majesty.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín fún funfun gba adé Ọbàtálá, gbogbo ibi di ìmọ́lẹ̀; ikú kì í pa awo funfun. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín shone in immaculate white and received the crown of Ọbàtálá, transforming all darkness into radiance; death never claims the pristine initiate: Announcing spiritual transfiguration.)

Àlà funfun kì í dọ̀tí lójú Ọlọ́run; ẹni tí ó mọ́ ọkàn ni àpótí ọlá. (White linen never soils before the Creator; he who maintains a clean conscience is the treasury of majesty: Praising moral purity.)

Ẹni tí ó ru ẹbọ Òfún ti di odi mọ́ gbogbo ibi; a kì í fi ìméjì bọ Òrìṣà. (He who makes the sacrifice of Òfún has walled off all wickedness; one must not serve the divinities with double-mindedness: Demanding sincere devotion.)
ODU_106_Ọ̀wọ́nrín_Òfún.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Idowu, E. Bolaji (1962). Olodumare: God in Yoruba Belief.

ODU_107_Ọ̀bàrà_Ogbè.historical_timeline: Classical Ilé-Ifẹ̀ Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀bàrà-Bogbè or Ọ̀bàrà-Ogbè, celebrated throughout Yorùbá civilization as the supreme chapter of royal oratory, poetic mastery, and sudden elevation from poverty to kingship. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́: Consulted by the Aláàfin and Ọ̀yọ́ Mèsì when ratifying new dynastic appointments. Transatlantic Lineage: Universally revered in Cuban Santería/Ifá as Obara Bogbe.
ODU_107_Ọ̀bàrà_Ogbè.etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀bàrà (kingship, royal manifestation, eloquent speech) on the right with Ogbè (cosmic light, supreme authority, expansion) on the left. Encapsulates the ultimate philosophical thesis of Yorùbá royal statecraft: truthful speech endowed with divine light elevates the poorest seeker to the palace throne.
ODU_107_Ọ̀bàrà_Ogbè.material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed upon Ọpọ́n Ifá in two vertical columns: I/II/II/II on the right for Ọ̀bàrà and I on the left for Ogbè. Prepared with Ewé Àkòko, Ewé Ẹ̀lẹ́gẹdẹ (pumpkin leaves), rooster, white cowries, and honey.
ODU_107_Ọ̀bàrà_Ogbè.social_and_ritual_context: Cast for princes awaiting coronation, scholars delivering major orations, and entrepreneurs seeking epochal breakthroughs. Prescribes absolute honesty, clearing debts, and charity to the vulnerable.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀bàrà bogbè sọ òtítọ́, ó di ọba lórí àléfà; ahọ́n rere ní ń fa adé wá. (Ọ̀bàrà Bogbè spoke the unyielding truth and ascended the ancestral throne; an eloquent, honest tongue is that which attracts the crown: Exalting truth-telling in royal leadership.)

Ẹni tí ayé kẹ́gàn ní àná ló ń jẹ oyè ńlá lónìí; Ifá kì í fi ọmọ olódodo sílẹ̀ láìní ẹ̀ṣọ́. (He whom the world mocked yesterday is invested with supreme chieftaincy today; Ifá never leaves the child of the righteous without majestic adornment: Offering solace against persecution.)

A kì í fi irọ́ kọ́ ààfin ọlá; òtítọ́ inú nìkan ló lè gbé adé dúró lórí awo. (One does not build the palace of majesty with lies; only inner truthfulness can sustain the crown upon the initiate's head: Mandating inviolable integrity for leaders.)
ODU_107_Ọ̀bàrà_Ogbè.provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Abiodun, Rowland (2014). Yoruba Art and Language.
